title: ISO metric screw threads: pitch, basic diameters, tap drill
notes: Coarse thread (Regelgewinde) is written without pitch: 'M8'. Fine thread (Feingewinde) carries the pitch: 'M8x1'.
Basic minor diameter of the internal thread D1 = d - 1.082532 * P (ISO 724).
Minor diameter of the external thread d3 = d - 1.226869 * P (ISO 724).
Pitch diameter d2 = D2 = d - 0.649519 * P (ISO 724).
Tap drill for coarse threads per ISO 2306 / DIN 336 (table below). For fine threads tap drill = d - P.
A threaded hole is modelled as its tap-drill core hole. A threaded shaft end is modelled at its nominal diameter d.
Drawing representation (ISO 6410): thick line = crest, thin line = root; in an end view the root is a 3/4 thin circle.

fine_pitches.comment: Preferred fine pitches (ISO 262). Any pitch is accepted by the lookup; these are used only to warn about unusual combinations.

blind_hole_rule_of_thumb.comment: Not a standard value. Usable thread depth is dimensioned on the drawing; if only the thread depth is given, the drill depth is commonly about thread depth + 3 * pitch (cone tip not included). Always flag such an assumption.
